newsitem.title: UK: LME metals whip back to close at fresh highs.
newsitem.headline: LME metals whip back to close at fresh highs.

text.p: The LME metals complex scored an impressive comeback by Wednesday's close, whipping back from a brief look at the downside to notch up fresh highs in copper and aluminium.
After prices slumped on Tuesday, traders and analysts expected the market to test the downside or at least consolidate for several days.
But after a quick probe lower in the morning, prices snapped back, led by nickel, forcing shorts to scramble to cover and sparking a widespread rally.
Nickel led the turnaround in the morning when unhappy workers at the huge Norilsk complex in Russia threatened to strike on March 15 over unpaid wages.

The slide in three month prices screeched to a halt at a low of $7,760 and emboldened the other metals to also reverse direction as funds and speculative players were forced to cover their short positions.
"Consumer buying, while not the main element, also added to the euphoria," said analyst Robin Bahr at broker Brandeis.
Nickel regained the $8,000 break-out point and finished just off its high at $8,050, a gain of $200 on the day.
If the market is able to hold above $8,000, it should be on track to rechallenge recent highs of $8,120, analysts said.
Above there were targets of $8,200, highs from May 1996 and $8,430, the May 14 peak.
Three months copper ended the kerb $42 higher at $2,392 per tonne, just $1 off its a fresh nine-month high, after sliding to a low of $2,335 in the morning.
Later, in inter-office trading the market shot up further to be bid above $2,400.
The next major chart level was seen at $2,434, the high of June 4, 1996, and a $2,450 technical target from an ascending triangle.
Wider spreads and borrowing of March/April gave an added boost to the market. The premium of cash over three months widened to $67/$70 from $60/65 on Tuesday.
Aluminium also scored fresh highs, hitting a 9-1/2 month peak of $1,665 and ending the kerb there, up $22 on the day.
Chartists peg the next significant level at $1,680, the high of May 1996.
Zinc also joined in the fun, regaining the $1,200 area and ending the kerb $14 higher at $1,222.
This put it on line to rechallenge the recent high of $1,235 and the January 1995 peak of $1,239, analysts said.
The other metals were less buoyant.
Lead ended $1 higher at $665 and tin showed independence by ignoring the gains in the others. It lost $69 to end the kerb at $5,841.
Alloy ended at $1,550/60, up from $1,540.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
